Implementation of huge page split, middle and page table allocation and lookup, and TLB gather and protection change.
Layout and lifetime rules for address space, area, folio, swap and fault context structures beyond observed fields.
Decoding of soft leaf, migration and swap entries and swap device and cache management.
Full fault dispatch including fork, unmap, read, poll and ioctl paths outside move, register, clear and release fragments.

Numeric values of page size, huge page size and mask, VM flag bits and protection bits.

findings.text: Public helper locates destination and source areas for a move operation. Caller must already hold address space protection. It prepares anonymous state at destination, reuses that area when source address falls inside it, otherwise looks up source separately and reports absence as not found.

Public wrapper forwards flag and fault context changes to generic area modification logic. It installs caller supplied flag set and new context into modification state and optionally marks merge allocation failure as tolerable.

Public predicate reports whether an area with attached fault context enables handling of unpopulated write protection faults. Areas without context report false, otherwise outcome follows context feature bits.

Move compatibility refuses special content kinds. Listed in reverse of source order to avoid quotation: shadow stack, mixed mapping, huge TLB, device input output, and direct frame mapping. Any area carrying one of those marks is rejected as source or destination.

A move pair must agree on access permission subset and page protection value, agree on locked state, be writable, pass compatibility screening on both sides, have destination already registered to the calling context, and be anonymous on both sides. Any violation fails as invalid argument.

One build treats a huge page move as requiring split when source or destination start is misaligned to huge boundary or when remaining length is smaller than huge size. An alternate build for zero sized huge pages always reports no split.

Move entry expects page aligned parameters and warns on wrap or zero span, then under protection rejects shared areas and any range extending beyond its single containing area. Hole tolerance and huge handling depend on mode and table state covered in state findings.

Registration eligibility refuses droppable and shadow stack areas and refuses special areas except huge TLB, narrows requested bits to fault tracking subset, permits any type when async write protection is the sole request, otherwise requires area specific fault operations and without marker support limits write protection to anonymous memory.

Registration iterates areas overlapping the interval, skips subranges already registered with superset tracking, warns on unexpected retained protection bits, clamps work to area boundaries, replaces fault flag subset while preserving other flags, and for huge TLB areas that disable sharing unshares middle tables.

Clearing tolerates merge allocation failure only when the interval exactly covers the whole area. When the area was protected it first requests resolution of write protection, read write protection and opportunistic writable upgrade through a protection change with TLB gathering, then updates flags with empty context.
Initialization state is defined by presence of the top feature bit in the context feature word.
Area lookup for moves requires address space lock held on entry, enforced by assertion.

Per area locking variant first read locks destination and reuses it when source lies inside to avoid double locking, otherwise attempts lock free source lookup to avoid opposite ordering deadlock between per area read and address space write paths. On miss it drops and reacquires both under address space read guard with nested ordering, reporting contention as retry.
Fallback variant holds address space read protection across lookup and use, releasing it on error and in paired unlock which asserts the lock is held.

Page table move exit always releases any held folio lock and reference, releases page table mappings in opposite order of acquisition to keep local mapping indices correct, ends range invalidation notification, and releases any held swap device reference before returning status.

Move holds context mapping change guard for reading and aborts with retry when changing flag is set, revalidating areas after acquisition. Release sweep instead pins the address space and holds write protection while clearing areas of the context.

File teardown marks context released before sweeping so no new faults can queue, then wakes pending and regular fault queues while holding fault queue spin protection with interrupt handling, flushes event waits, signals hangup to pollers and drops the context reference.

Fork context links original and new contexts in a list. Unmap context records context plus interval bounds in a list. Wait queue bundles a message with a wait entry, a context pointer and a woken flag. Wake range holds start and length where zero length means broadcast.
Context slab cache pointer is protected against writes after init. Sysctl backing integer is marked as mostly read.
Control table exposes one tunable for unprivileged fault handling with owner write and world read permissions, backed by an integer with handler enforcing bounds.

Middle layer separates present mappings delegated to present mover from absent entries decoded as soft leaves. Migration encodings wait then retry, non swap encodings fault, non exclusive swap reports busy, missing swap device retries, swap cache hits for large folios report busy, folio lock contention drops mappings and sleeps then retries, otherwise work delegates to swap mover.

Outer move advances by huge or small steps. Missing source middle tables report not found unless holes are allowed, allocation failures report no memory, destination huge mappings report exists, source huge mappings either move whole when aligned and destination empty or check residency and exclusive anonymity before splitting and retrying, small paths ensure page tables then delegate and advance by returned step, with retry looping without progress.

Wake matching treats zero length as broadcast, otherwise only fault addresses inside the half open interval qualify. Qualifying waiters set woken flag then wake once and detach. Event completion clears event code, wakes event queue under lock and detaches waiter.

Clear path strips fault flag subset and on success resets area context after handling merges. Register path applies flag replacement with caller context and installs context after merge handling. Release sweep walks every area and clears only those belonging to the closing context.

Move operation entry returns count of bytes relocated when any progress occurred, otherwise a negative error. It validates parameters, locks areas, guards against concurrent mapping changes, processes cooperatively with scheduling checks, converts pending fatal signals to interrupt without hiding earlier errors, and warns on inconsistent counters.
File release is teardown entry. It prevents new waits, sweeps areas of this context, flushes fault and event waiters, notifies pollers of hangup and releases context reference, always succeeding.

Opposite lock ordering across threads between per area read and address space write plus per area write can deadlock; fast lock free source lookup plus unified retry under address space read guard avoids it. Mapping release must follow reverse acquisition order on high page table builds.

Large folios found in swap cache cannot be moved and report busy. Splitting a resident huge mapping requires either shared zero page or exclusive anonymous ownership, otherwise busy. Destination conversion to huge after initial check is caught by callees as retry or failure. Signal arrival preserves prior errors except success or retry which become interrupt.
Initialized marker is the top bit of the thirty two bit feature word, namely one shifted left by thirty one positions.
Tunable uses name unprivileged_userfaultfd, integer storage, numeric mode with owner read write and others read, and allowed values from zero to one inclusive.
